newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn coalition agrees pension plan-labour minister.
newsitem.headline: Bonn coalition agrees pension plan-labour minister.

text.p: The ruling coalition's pension experts agreed on a plan to reform Germany's generous pension system over the next 20 years, Labour Minister Norbert Bluem said on Sunday.
Bluem, after a closed pension planning session here, declined to provide any details but said the plan would be turned over to coalition leaders.
Chancellor Helmut Kohl's ruling coalition has twice put off a decision on pensions -- embarrassing Bluem, his longest-serving minister, who has championed an overhaul.

Bluem has sought to cut pension contributions to below 20 percent of wages, from the current 20.3 percent level. He also wanted to lower pension benefits to 64 percent of average net wages after 45 years of work -- down from 70 percent today.
